category_title: Students with severe hearing impairment and EAL who use physical gestures and lip-reading to decipher archaic language
minimal_context: The student is rehearsing a script aloud for an upcoming drama performance.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's practice reading your script aloud for the final performance.

STUDENT: (Enthusiastically gets into character, putting his hand to his ear) I hear... (Uses pointing and punching actions while reading, having great difficulty pronouncing the words)

TUTOR: Good effort. Make sure you pronounce the 's' sounds at the end of the words.

STUDENT: (Perseveres and continues reading aloud with confidence, still missing the 's' sounds)

TUTOR: You missed the 's' sounds again. Please listen to my suggestion and try to fix your pronunciation.

STUDENT: (Ignores the suggestions completely, acting as though he is doing it right, and continues reading his lines undeterred)

options.A: Maintain a high ratio of praise to error correction statements during script rehearsals.
options.B: Implement relatively tight timelines for completing the script reading and drama activities.
options.C: Implement a daily point system for rehearsals, setting a goal of 80% of possible points.
options.D: Provide increased autonomy, collaboration, and engagement in drama-focused activities during rehearsals.
